findings.title: [intake] What data accompanies a read of an address the register map does not declare?
findings.detail: csr_register_map.unmapped_read_data is not stated. A spec-derived model and a design can both be 'correct' with different answers; the comparison is unfalsifiable until this is stated. Disposition: decision — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: VP_CSR_006 — design returned 0xDEADBEEF, model returned 0; waived as W-001.

findings.title: [intake] What happens on a write to an undeclared address — error flag, silent drop, or both?
findings.detail: csr_register_map.unmapped_write_behavior is not stated. Error-flag comparison on unmapped writes rests on an assumption. Disposition: decision — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: sibling of VP_CSR_006 (the error flag happened to agree; the spec never said it must).

findings.title: [intake] Do byte enables mean anything on a READ, and what value is expected on the request?
findings.detail: csr_register_map.read_byte_enable_semantics is not stated. A model predicted full enables on reads; the bus drove none. Neither is wrong. Disposition: decision — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: byte_enable_semantics finding (path_18).

findings.title: [intake] When a status register is read in the same cycle its source changes, does the read return the old or the new value?
findings.detail: csr_register_map.status_read_sampling is not stated. A one-cycle coincidence produced a mismatch that no waiver can express. Registered designs return the old value; the spec must say so. Disposition: decision — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: csr_status_read_coherency finding (path_12/13, CTRL_STATUS.ref_pending_cnt).

findings.title: [intake] On the DDR channel, does the data-mask pin mask or enable a byte?
findings.detail: data_path_mapping.ddr_dm_polarity is not stated. The design drives ~sel (JEDEC-correct); a spec-derived model carried sel through unchanged. The standard decides this one. The applicable standard (JESD79-3 (DDR3)) answers this: active_high_mask — DM=1 masks the byte. The host-side wishbone sel (1 = write this byte) is the inverse convention. Validation adopts that value and keeps checking; please state it in the spec. First encountered as: byte_enable_semantics finding (data_path pack/unpack gate).

findings.title: [intake] Does the failure taxonomy have ids for what a queue + arbiter can do wrong — drop a request, invent a command, starve a refresh?
findings.detail: no failure_taxonomy id starts with 'SCHED_'; needed for: dropped request, invented command, refresh never serviced. Checkers reported real defects under locally proposed ids (SCHED_001..003) that the spec cannot name. Disposition: vocabulary — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: taxonomy_gap finding (stage invariant checkers).

findings.title: [intake] For every pair of blocks a path connects, what are the port-level signals, widths and handshake between them?
findings.detail: spec has no 'block_interfaces' section; 19 block-to-block hops are declared by path_definitions and none has an interface contract. The drop shipped 11 blocks and no top level; two block pairs did not compose (no bank on cmd_gen's feedback, nothing consuming calibration's ZQCS request). Validation had to author a 75-connection map by hand. Interfaces that are not specified cannot be generated consistently on both sides. Disposition: decision — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: integration_map.json glue entries; fb-bank and ZQCS findings.

findings.title: [intake] Does the failure taxonomy have an id for violating EVERY timing parameter the timing model states?
findings.detail: failure_taxonomy names no failure for ['tREFI']; every stated timing parameter needs a violation id. A parameter with no failure id has no assertion name to report under; tREFI had none, so the refresh-interval assertion reports under a proposed TIMING_012. Disposition: vocabulary — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: sva_rules.json max_interval_rules (tREFI) — no taxonomy id names tREFI.

findings.title: [intake] What is the minimum spacing between consecutive mode-register-set commands (tMRD)?
findings.detail: timing_model.tMRD is not stated. The init sequence issues four MRS commands; without tMRD their spacing cannot be asserted, so INIT_002 is only partially checkable. The applicable standard (JESD79-3 (DDR3)) answers this: 4 nCK — MRS-to-MRS command spacing. Stated in nanoseconds in timing_model (4 x tCK). Validation adopts that value and keeps checking; please state it in the spec. First encountered as: sva_rules.json command_groups[init] — only tZQinit could be generated.

findings.title: [intake] What is the minimum delay from a mode-register-set command to the next non-MRS command (tMOD)?
findings.detail: timing_model.tMOD is not stated. ZQCL after the last MRS cannot be checked for tMOD without it. The applicable standard (JESD79-3 (DDR3)) answers this: max(12 nCK, 15 ns) — MRS to any non-MRS command. Validation adopts that value and keeps checking; please state it in the spec. First encountered as: sva_rules.json command_groups[init].
